⭐STAR StoryPART 2 OF 3›02
S

Situation — Why was the pipeline needed?

Start with the business background, not the code.

Business context

The Data Engineering team needed to prepare HDB resale-flat data for the Data Science team.

The required period was January 2012 to December 2016.

Data challenge

The input was a ZIP containing multiple CSV files, and older files could have missing columns.

The solution had to preserve original files and avoid manual changes or hard-coded processing.

Situation memory: Multiple files + inconsistent schemas + strict business rules + auditable outputs.
T

Task — What did I need to deliver?

Turn the assignment into four engineering objectives.

01Preserve & Combine

Keep source files unchanged and union schemas into one staging dataset.

02Validate & Clean

Standardise fields, recompute lease, deduplicate and identify review cases.

03Transform & Protect

Create the prescribed identifier and generate its SHA-256 representation.

04Explain & Reconcile

Produce profiles, failure reasons, row counts, tests and a run manifest.

Senior-level framing

The task was not only to clean a CSV. It was to create a repeatable data product with clear modules, deterministic rules, separate exception paths, and reconciliation evidence.

A

Action — How did I implement it?

This is the longest part of the answer. Follow the six numbered steps.

1

Ingest, preserve and profile

The pipeline opens the ZIP programmatically, discovers contributing CSV files and filters the required date range.

It performs a schema union: columns missing from older files are added as null so all records share one master schema.

Profiling records null counts, null percentages, data types, distinct counts and key categorical distributions.

2

Validate and standardise

Rules cover month, town, flat type, flat model, storey range, block, street, floor area, lease year and resale price.

Invalid records are removed from the accepted flow and written to Failed with an explicit failure reason.

3

Recalculate remaining lease

I use a 99-year lease, the lease commencement year and a configurable as_of_date.

The configurable date makes results reproducible instead of changing every time the pipeline runs.

lease_end = lease_commence_date + 99 yearsremaining = floor(lease_end − as_of_date) → years + months
4

Resolve duplicate transactions deterministically

The composite key uses all original business columns except resale_price.

For the same key, I retain the highest price and send lower-priced records to Failed as DUPLICATE_LOWER_PRICE.

Same composite key?→Sort price descending→Rank 1: keepRank >1: Failed
5

Flag unusual resale prices with IQR

First, I calculate price_per_sqm = resale_price / floor_area_sqm so flats of different sizes are comparable.

I compare similar flats within the same year, town, and flat type.

Q125th percentile
IQRQ3 − Q1
LowerQ1 − 1.5 × IQR
UpperQ3 + 1.5 × IQR

IQR measures the spread of the middle 50 percent of the price_per_sqm values.

Values outside the 1.5-times-IQR bounds are flagged for Review, but not automatically rejected.

A flagged record remains in Cleaned and is also copied to Review, because unusual does not automatically mean invalid.

Q
Why did you choose IQR, and where does the 1.5 come from?
A

I chose IQR (Interquartile Range) because it is simple, explainable, and robust to extreme values. The 1.5-times-IQR threshold is a standard Tukey rule for flagging outliers.

6

Create the identifier and hash

After quality rules, the pipeline builds the required identifier: S + BBB + AA + MM + T.

SBBBAAMMT
S fixed prefix
BBB first three block digits, left-padded
AA first two digits of grouped average price
MM transaction month
T first town character

The clear identifier is written to Transformed, while Hashed contains its irreversible SHA-256 value encoded from UTF-8.

Because the prescribed identifier uses shortened grouped attributes, it is not guaranteed to be a transaction-level unique key.

🧩Core Rules, Code & OutputsPART 3 OF 3›03

Core rules — the five points most likely to be questioned

RuleImplementationWhy
Schema differencesUnion all source columns; missing historical fields become null.Preserves every source attribute without manual edits.
Remaining lease99-year lease + configurable as_of_date; round down to years and months.Reproducible and aligned with the requirement.
DuplicatesComposite business key excludes price; highest price survives.Deterministic and auditable resolution.
Price anomalyPrice/sqm, grouped by year-town-flat type, 1.5×IQR bounds.Creates comparable peer groups and avoids treating review cases as invalid.
IdentifierS + BBB + AA + MM + T, then SHA-256.Follows the prescribed transformation and irreversible hashing requirement.

Code structure — how the design stays maintainable

I organised the implementation as a small Python package rather than placing every rule in one notebook or script.

src/hdb_pipeline/
├── main.py             # Command-line entry point
├── config.py           # Pipeline configuration
├── ingestion.py        # Source discovery, extraction and schema union
├── data_quality.py     # Profiling, validation, lease, deduplication and anomaly detection
├── transformation.py   # Resale Identifier creation and SHA-256 hashing
├── output.py           # Output datasets and run manifest
└── pipeline.py         # End-to-end ETL orchestration
main.pyParse CLI arguments
→
pipeline.pyControl the complete ETL sequence
↓
config.pyPaths, as-of date and parameters
ingestion.pyZIP → CSV discovery → schema union
data_quality.pyProfile → validate → lease → deduplicate → IQR
transformation.pyIdentifier → SHA-256
↓
output.pyWrite datasets, manifest and reconciliation evidence
How to explain the diagram: pipeline.py is deliberately thin. It coordinates the sequence, while each specialist module owns one category of responsibility. This reduces coupling and lets validation, transformation or output logic be tested and changed independently.
Single responsibilityEach module owns one clear concern.
Configuration-drivenNo business date is hidden inside rule logic.
TestableRules can be unit-tested without running the full pipeline.
AuditableOutputs, failure reasons and manifest explain every run.
R

Presentation-ready STAR answer

Situation: HDB needed a programmatic and reproducible way to prepare multiple resale-flat files from 2012–2016 for analysis.

Task: I had to preserve raw data, enforce data quality and business rules, create the prescribed identifier and produce auditable outputs.

Action: I separated the pipeline into ingestion, data quality, transformation, output and orchestration modules. I unioned changing schemas, profiled and validated data, recalculated the 99-year remaining lease with a configurable as-of date, kept the higher price for duplicate business keys, and applied peer-group IQR to price per square metre for review cases. Finally, I generated the identifier and SHA-256 hash.

Result: The pipeline produces Raw, Staging, Profiling, Cleaned, Failed, Review, Transformed and Hashed outputs, together with a run manifest, reconciliation counts and automated tests.

30-second memory:Preserve → Profile → Validate → Lease → Deduplicate → Review → Identify → Hash → Reconcile.

AWS batch data ingestion architecture

EventBridge Scheduler starts the Step Functions workflow.
02
Step Functions runs the downloader, a Python application packaged as a Docker container, on ECS Fargate.

CloudWatch collects logs and metrics, while Amazon SNS sends failure notifications.
🔐Network, Large Files & SecurityPART 2 OF 3›02
🔐

Network, Large Files & Security

PART 2 OF 3

These three design considerations explain how the ingestion path stays private where possible, handles large files, and remains production-oriented.

🌐

Network

Fargate stays in a private subnet with no public IP. Public HTTPS access to data.gov.sg goes through the NAT Gateway.

S3 traffic uses the S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint, so AWS storage access stays on a private path.

📦

Large files

The downloader streams the source and uses multipart upload instead of loading the whole file into memory.

SHA-256 metadata provides an integrity fingerprint for traceability and duplicate checks.

🛡️

Security & operations

Step Functions starts Glue only after the download and S3 upload succeed; failures can be retried cleanly.

CloudWatch provides logs and operational visibility, while IAM and encryption protect access to the data.

Data Ingestion — Key Q&A

CORE 7

7 high-probability questions covering orchestration, compute choice, private access, large-file handling, reliability, and service boundaries.

🧭
Control flowEventBridge = when; Step Functions = what happens next.
🔐
NetworkPublic source via NAT; S3 via Gateway Endpoint.
📦
ResponsibilityFargate moves; Glue transforms.

🧭
Architecture & computeOrchestration, service boundaries, and why Fargate / Glue are separated.
3 Qs⌄
QPointANotes
01Why do you need Step Functions?HIGHStep Functions = what happens next.
Step Functions orchestrates the workflow: start Fargate, wait for completion, verify success, and then start Glue.
It also gives me retry, catch, and an explicit failure path.
Emphasise sequencing and failure control.
02Why Fargate instead of Lambda?HIGHLarge file + runtime control → Fargate.
The source can be larger than 100 MB and download duration is less predictable.
Fargate gives more control over runtime, memory, container dependencies, and streaming large files.
Lambda is better for shorter, lighter workloads.
Do not claim Lambda cannot handle 100 MB; frame this as workload fit.
03Why use Glue instead of doing transformation inside Fargate?HIGHFargate moves; Glue transforms.
I separate acquisition from transformation.
Fargate is responsible for reliable external download; Glue is the scalable ETL service that integrates naturally with S3 and the Glue Data Catalog.
Single responsibility makes support easier.
🔐
Network & private accessPrivate-subnet egress, NAT, and the S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint.
2 Qs⌄
QPointANotes
04If Fargate has no public IP, how can it access data.gov.sg?HIGHPrivate subnet → NAT → IGW → public source.
The private subnet route sends internet-bound traffic to a NAT Gateway in a public subnet.
The NAT Gateway then reaches data.gov.sg through the Internet Gateway.
NAT provides outbound connectivity, not inbound exposure.
05Why do you still need the S3 Gateway Endpoint if you already have NAT?HIGHPublic source via NAT; S3 via Gateway Endpoint.
NAT is needed for the public data.gov.sg endpoint.
S3 is an AWS service, so I use an S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint to keep S3 traffic on the AWS network and avoid unnecessary NAT usage.
Separate internet egress from AWS service access.
🛡️
Large files & reliabilityStreaming, multipart upload, failure handling, and sequencing.
2 Qs⌄
QPointANotes
06How do you support files larger than 100 MB?HIGHStream → hash → multipart upload.
The downloader streams the HTTPS response in chunks, updates SHA-256 incrementally, and uploads to S3 Raw with multipart upload rather than loading the whole object into memory.
Memory usage should not grow with file size.
07What happens if the Fargate download fails?HIGHDownload fails → no Glue.
Glue must not start.
Step Functions retries transient errors where appropriate and, after retries are exhausted, routes to the failure path.
Never process a partial or failed acquisition.

Private Access & VPC Design

Three practical controls keep the analytics path private, governed, and easy to explain.

Private Tableau accessAthena Interface EndpointS3 Gateway EndpointClear VPC boundary

Private Access & VPC Design

👤

Private entry

Internal users reach Tableau on EC2 through the approved corporate network or VPN. The EC2 instance stays in a private analytics subnet with no public IP.

🔒

Private Athena API path

Tableau uses the Athena JDBC or ODBC driver. The Athena Interface VPC Endpoint with Private DNS keeps the API call private.

🗂️

Data, metadata & VPC boundary

Athena uses Glue Data Catalog metadata to query processed Parquet in S3, and query-result S3 access can use the S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint.

Separate application and analytics VPCs are a design choice for clearer isolation; a shared VPC with separate subnets is also valid for a smaller environment.

Data Exploitation — Key Q&A

7 high-probability questions covering Athena, Tableau integration, Glue Catalog, private endpoints, performance, and query governance.

Layer rolesS3 stores; Glue describes; Athena queries; Tableau visualises.

4 Qs⌄
QPointANotes
01Why Athena?HIGHS3 data + on-demand SQL → Athena.
The processed data already lives in S3.
Athena provides serverless SQL directly on S3, so I avoid operating a persistent database cluster for an intermittent analytical workload.
Frame this as a workload-fit decision.
02Why does Tableau connect through Athena instead of directly to S3?HIGHS3 stores; Glue describes; Athena queries; Tableau visualises.
Tableau needs a SQL query layer rather than raw object storage.
Athena provides SQL semantics and Glue Catalog provides schema and partition metadata.
This is the single best component-responsibility memory line.
03What is the role of Glue Data Catalog here?HIGHGlue Catalog = metadata, not data.
Glue Data Catalog stores metadata such as database, table, columns, data types, S3 location, and partitions.
It does not store the HDB data itself.
Keep storage and metadata separate.
04Why is Tableau Server on EC2, while the downloader uses Fargate?HIGHShort-lived batch → Fargate; long-running stateful server → EC2.
I used Fargate for the downloader because it is a short-lived batch task.
Tableau Server is a long-running, stateful application that requires persistent storage, stable compute and operating-system-level administration, so EC2 is more appropriate.
High-priority workload-fit question: compare lifecycle, state and administration needs.
⚡
Performance & costConnect Parquet, partitioning, and Athena scan cost.
1 Q⌄
QPointANotes
05Why use Parquet and time-based partitions for Athena?HIGHParquet + partitions = less scan, faster queries, lower cost.
Parquet is columnar and compressed, so Athena can scan only the columns a query needs.
Partitioning by year and transaction_month lets Athena prune unrelated S3 prefixes when time filters are used.
Together, they reduce scanned bytes, improve performance, and lower query cost.
Tie physical data layout directly to Athena performance and cost.
🔐
Private networkingExplain private API access and endpoint types without confusing the control plane with S3 data access.
2 Qs⌄
QPointANotes
06Why does Athena need an Interface VPC Endpoint?HIGHTableau → Athena API via Interface Endpoint.
Tableau runs in a private subnet.
The Athena Interface VPC Endpoint gives Tableau a private path to the Athena API without sending that API traffic through the public internet.
This addresses the test requirement directly.
07Why Interface Endpoint for Athena but Gateway Endpoint for S3?HIGHS3 = Gateway; Athena = Interface.
S3 supports Gateway Endpoints through route tables.
Athena exposes service APIs through an Interface Endpoint, which creates private ENIs inside the VPC.
Know the endpoint type difference.
🛡️
Governance & trade-offsShow query governance and when another warehouse such as Redshift would be a better fit.
1 Q⌄
QPointANotes
08What is an Athena Workgroup?HIGHWorkgroup = query governance.
A Workgroup is a governance boundary for Athena queries.
It can enforce result location, encryption, query settings, and cost controls for a set of users or workloads.
One of the highest-probability questions.

AWS Design

FLOW
Schedule → Orchestrate → Ingest → Transform → Store & Catalog → Query → Present
AWS
EventBridge → Step Functions → (Fargate > S3 Raw) → Glue → (S3 Processed + Glue Catalog) → Athena → Tableau
01 · SCHEDULE
EventBridge Scheduler decides when the workflow starts.
02 · ORCHESTRATE
Step Functions controls the workflow order, waits for dependencies, and handles retries or failure paths.
03 · INGEST
ECS Fargate runs the downloader container and writes the source data into S3 Raw.
04 · TRANSFORM
AWS Glue reads the raw data, applies the ETL logic, and prepares the processed datasets.
05 · STORE & CATALOG
S3 Processed stores the transformed Parquet data, while the Glue Data Catalog stores table, schema, and partition metadata.
06 · QUERY
Athena uses the catalog metadata to query the required processed data in S3.
07 · PRESENT
Tableau sends SQL through Athena and presents the returned results as dashboards and visualisations.
LINE :
Schedule → Orchestrate → Ingest → Transform → Store & Catalog → Query → Present

Lambda is serverless compute that runs code in response to events without managing servers.
Used for
Use it for short event-driven tasks such as reacting to an S3 upload, validating metadata, or starting the next processing step.
Key point
Choose Lambda when the workload is event-driven and fits its execution model; use Fargate when the workload needs a longer-running container with more predictable resources.
🪣

Amazon S3

What it is
S3 is durable object storage for documents, raw files, intermediate artefacts, model inputs, and processed outputs.
Used for
In a document-intelligence flow, S3 is commonly the landing zone for uploaded PDFs or images and the shared storage layer between services.
Key point
S3 stores the objects; downstream services such as Textract, OpenSearch, and SageMaker process or consume the data.
📄

Amazon Textract

What it is
Textract is a managed document-analysis service that extracts text, forms, tables, and structured information from scanned documents and images.
Used for
Use it to convert PDFs or document images into machine-readable text and key-value information before search, analytics, or ML processing.
Key point
Textract performs document extraction; it is not the search engine and it is not the model-training platform.
🔎

Amazon OpenSearch Service

What it is
OpenSearch Service is a managed search and analytics engine for indexing documents and supporting low-latency search and retrieval.
Used for
Use it to index extracted document content so applications can perform keyword, filtered, or retrieval-oriented searches over processed documents.
Key point
OpenSearch is the retrieval/search layer; S3 remains the object store and Textract remains the extraction layer.
🤖

Amazon SageMaker

What it is
SageMaker is a managed platform for building, training, tuning, and deploying machine-learning models.
Used for
Use it when the workflow needs model training, inference endpoints, batch inference, experiments, or managed ML lifecycle capabilities.
Key point
SageMaker is the ML layer; it consumes prepared data rather than replacing ingestion, document extraction, or search services.
LINE :
Lambda → S3 → Textract → OpenSearch → SageMaker
🧩H Knowledge & Q&A›03
🌐

Private Networking — NAT Gateway vs VPC Endpoint

Use these two diagrams to explain where traffic goes from a private Fargate task.

Line : Download via NAT; then upload to S3 through the VPC Endpoint.

1. Public download path

The private Fargate task initiates HTTPS through NAT Gateway and Internet Gateway. The response returns through the same path and lands back on Fargate.

2. Private upload to S3 Raw

After Fargate receives the file, it streams or multipart-uploads it to S3 Raw through the S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint. This path does not use NAT or the public internet.

DownloadFargate → NAT Gateway → Internet Gateway → data.gov.sg → back to Fargate
UploadFargate → S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint → S3 Raw
LineNAT = internet; VPC Endpoint = private AWS service access
📦

ECS + Fargate — Mental Model

ECS orchestrates the containers; Fargate provides the serverless compute that runs the tasks.

Line :ECS = orchestrator → Fargate = compute → Task = running container workload

How it applies to this project

ECSdefines and orchestrates the batch task.
Fargateruns the Downloader container without managing EC2 worker nodes.
Why this choicethe workload is a simple batch container job, so EKS would add unnecessary Kubernetes complexity.
📊

Tableau + Athena — Query Path

One sentence to remember: Tableau presents; Athena queries.

TABLEAU
Tableau EC2 is the BI layer. It sends SQL through the Athena JDBC driver.
PRIVATE API
Athena Interface VPC Endpoint keeps the API call private inside the VPC.
QUERY
Athena reads metadata from Glue Data Catalog and scans S3 Processed.
RESULT
Athena writes output to S3 Query Results, then Tableau visualises the result.

01
HIGHEVENTBRIDGE · STEP FUNCTIONS · ECS FARGATE

AWS Orchestration & Containers

›
What it is
EventBridge Scheduler decides when to start. Step Functions coordinates the workflow. ECS Fargate runs the containerised downloader.
How to use it
Use Step Functions when multiple dependent AWS stages need retries, status tracking and failure handling. Use Fargate for a container workload without managing EC2 worker nodes.
Common Commands
# Start a Step Functions execution manually
aws stepfunctions start-execution --state-machine-arn <STATE_MACHINE_ARN> --name test-run

# List ECS tasks in a cluster
aws ecs list-tasks --cluster <CLUSTER_NAME>

# Describe a running or failed ECS task
aws ecs describe-tasks --cluster <CLUSTER_NAME> --tasks <TASK_ARN>

# Start a Glue job manually
aws glue start-job-run --job-name <GLUE_JOB_NAME>

# Tail CloudWatch logs
aws logs tail <LOG_GROUP_NAME> --follow
MEMORY
EventBridge = WHEN. Step Functions = WHAT NEXT. Fargate = WHERE THE CONTAINER RUNS.
Key Q&A
Q
Why EventBridge → Step Functions → Fargate?
PointWHEN → orchestration → compute.
A
EventBridge schedules the workflow. Step Functions coordinates dependent stages and retries. Fargate executes the downloader container.
Q
Why Fargate instead of Lambda?
PointLarge or long-running container batch workload.
A
Fargate gives fewer runtime constraints and a cleaner container execution model for potentially large downloads.
Q
Why Fargate instead of EC2 or EKS?
PointLess operations, less platform complexity.
A
EC2 adds worker-server management. EKS adds Kubernetes complexity that is unnecessary for a simple batch task.
02
HIGHENTERPRISE SCALE

Lakehouse, Iceberg & Data Platform

›
What a lakehouse means
A lakehouse keeps data in low-cost lake storage, then adds managed tables, governance, and SQL analytics on top.
🪣
LAKE STORAGE
Amazon S3
cheap · scalable · open files
+
🧊
TABLE SEMANTICS
Apache Iceberg
snapshot · ACID · schema evolution
+
🛡️
GOVERNANCE
Catalog + Access
permissions · lineage · ownership
+
⚡
SQL ENGINES
Athena / Spark SQL
interactive analytics
01 · S3
S3 stores the physical files. It is the storage foundation of the lakehouse.
02 · ICEBERG
Iceberg makes the files behave like a table. It adds snapshots, ACID transactions, and evolution features.
03 · GOVERNANCE
Governance answers who can use the data and how it is controlled. Think catalog, permissions, lineage, and ownership.
04 · SQL
Athena and Spark SQL query the managed tables directly. That gives warehouse-style analytics without moving the data out of the lake.
MEMORY
Lakehouse = S3 + Iceberg + Governance + SQL.
Key Q&A
Q
What makes this a lakehouse rather than just S3 storage?
PointStorage alone is not a lakehouse.
A
At enterprise scale, add table semantics such as Iceberg, metadata/catalog, governance, ownership, quality controls and self-service access.
Q
Parquet vs Iceberg?
PointFile format vs table format.
A
Parquet stores columnar data inside files. Iceberg manages a logical table across many files and adds snapshots and evolution capabilities.
Q
Pipeline vs Data Platform?
PointOne flow vs reusable capabilities for many teams.
A
A platform standardises common engineering capabilities so teams do not rebuild ingestion, governance and monitoring from scratch.
03
HIGHJD REQUIREMENT

Terraform & Infrastructure as Code

›
What it is
Terraform is declarative Infrastructure as Code. Infrastructure is described in HCL and Terraform tracks managed resources through state.
Why use it
IaC makes infrastructure repeatable, version controlled, reviewable, auditable and consistent across environments.
Common Commands
# Initialise the working directory, backend, providers and modules
terraform init

# Format Terraform files
terraform fmt

# Validate configuration
terraform validate

# Preview infrastructure changes
terraform plan -out=tfplan

# Apply the saved plan
terraform apply tfplan

# List resources tracked in state
terraform state list

# Show output values
terraform output

# Destroy managed infrastructure — use carefully
terraform destroy
Terraform

HCL · multi-provider ecosystem · explicit state · plan/apply

CloudFormation

YAML/JSON · AWS-native · stack-based state model · Change Sets

MEMORY
Terraform workflow = WRITE → INIT → VALIDATE → PLAN → APPLY.
Key Q&A
Q
Why Terraform / IaC?
PointRepeatable, reviewable and auditable infrastructure.
A
IaC reduces configuration drift, makes environment changes visible in version control and allows changes to be reviewed before deployment.
Q
What is Terraform state?
PointTerraform's mapping between configuration and real resources.
A
State lets Terraform understand what it already manages and calculate the next change. Team environments usually keep it in a controlled remote backend.
Q
Terraform vs CloudFormation?
PointMulti-provider IaC workflow vs AWS-native stack-based IaC.
A
Choose based on organisational standards, cloud scope and operational model rather than personal preference.
